timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So this is a quick video responding to Fudmonton's video posted yesterday asking to photograph Orion.
And this is a photograph I took about half an hour ago from where I live in San Francisco.
It's a little bit tough to photograph Orion because it's so low in horizon, but it is visible in the northern hemisphere just after sunset.
And this is of the photographs I took. The best one, Beetlejuice is clearly visible.
That's one of the shoulders of Orion. Bellatrix is the other. And the three stars of Orion's belt are also visible, although the right most one is pretty hard to see.
If we look at this in the online planetarium in the sky.org, we can see a schematic view of this where again, Orion's belt and both of its shoulders should be above the horizon.
So as long as you're viewing conditions are good, you should be able to see them.
I think that Fudmonton meant to ask this question in July. Here we see the planetarium's view of what sunrise will look like in July.
And at that time, when the sun rises, Orion's belt will just be rising then, and therefore Orion's belt will not be visible at night.
And when the sun sets, Orion's belt will already have set in the northern hemisphere.
So in July, it will not be possible to see Orion in the northern hemisphere, but in May, it is still possible.
